title: What's Wrong?
description: Describe common symptoms and answer basic follow-up questions.
objectives: Describe common symptoms and answer basic follow-up questions.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to describe common symptoms and answer basic follow-up questions. The central language is have plus symptom and feel plus adjective. It belongs to the practical context of health & everyday problems. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: have plus symptom and feel plus adjective

blocks.english: I have a sore throat and a cough.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the what's wrong? exchange.
This what's wrong? model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the what's wrong? exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I have a sore throat and a cough.” and “I've felt tired since yesterday.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: have plus symptom and feel plus adjective.
